title: The Lion's Share
summary: The Lion, the Fox, the Jackal, and the Wolf agreed to form a solemn hunting alliance, swearing upon their honor to share equally whatever game they brought down in the wilderness....
full_text:
The Lion, the Fox, the Jackal, and the Wolf agreed to form a solemn hunting alliance, swearing upon their honor to share equally whatever game they brought down in the wilderness.

After a long chase through the rocky gorges, the four companions managed to trap and bring down a magnificent, fat stag. The hunters gathered around the quarry, licking their chops in anticipation of a grand feast.

The Lion, assuming the mantle of leadership, raised his paw and commanded: "Cut the stag into four equal quarters, so that justice may be preserved among partners."

The wolf and jackal carved the carcass into four identical shares with great care. The Lion stood before the four portions, cleared his throat with a rumbling growl, and began his royal distribution:

"The first quarter belongs to me by right of my royal title, for I am sovereign of all the beasts of the forest. The second quarter falls to me on account of my superior strength and valor, since it was my claw that struck down the stag. The third quarter is mine because I contributed the greatest endurance to the hunt. And as for the fourth quarter," growled the Lion, baring his razor-sharp fangs and unsheathing his massive claws, "whoever among you dares to lay a single paw upon it must first defeat me in mortal combat!"

The Fox, the Jackal, and the Wolf exchanged silent, rueful glances, tucked their tails between their legs, and slunk away into the bushes with empty bellies, having learned the harsh lesson that an alliance with a tyrant always ends with the tyrant taking everything.
moral: Partnership with the powerful rarely brings equal rewards to the weak.
